categories.name: Regulatory
categories.subtitle: rules you must obey
categories.blurb: White and red signs state traffic laws. Ignoring them is a violation.

categories.name: Warning
categories.subtitle: hazards ahead
categories.blurb: Yellow diamonds warn about hazards on the road ahead. Slow down and be ready to react.

categories.name: Guide & services
categories.subtitle: directions & facilities
categories.blurb: Blue and green signs give directions, distances and available services along the route.

categories.name: Highway & exits
categories.subtitle: freeway guidance
categories.blurb: Green panels guide you along freeways: exits, lane assignments and destinations.

categories.name: Work zone
categories.subtitle: construction areas
categories.blurb: Orange signs mark construction zones. Fines are doubled where workers are present.

signs.name: Stop
signs.description: The only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or the edge of the intersection.
steps: Stop fully before the limit line or crosswalk
Look left, right, then left again
Go only when the intersection is clear and it is your turn
signs.trap: Rolling through slowly is still a violation — the exam always requires a complete stop, even with no traffic in sight.

signs.name: Yield
signs.description: Slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians on the road you are entering or crossing go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.
steps: Ease off the gas early
Give the right-of-way to cross traffic and pedestrians
Stop fully if you cannot merge or cross safely
signs.trap: Yield does not automatically mean stop — but answers claiming you never have to stop at a yield sign are wrong.

signs.name: Do not enter
signs.description: Traffic may not pass this point in your direction. It typically guards the exit end of freeway ramps and one-way streets.
steps: Do not drive past the sign
Check whether you are facing an off-ramp or one-way street
Turn around safely or choose another route
signs.trap: Do Not Enter is posted at the entrance; if you also see Wrong Way, you have already entered against traffic.

signs.name: Speed limit 55
signs.description: The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions is 55 mph. Rain, fog, or heavy traffic can make a lower speed the legal limit.
steps: Check your speedometer
Adjust to 55 mph or less
Slow below the limit when conditions are poor
signs.trap: A posted limit is a maximum, not a guaranteed safe speed — under the basic speed law, 55 can be illegal in bad weather.

signs.name: No U-turn
signs.description: U-turns are prohibited at this location. Continue on and find a legal place to reverse direction.
steps: Do not swing into a U-turn here
Continue to the next legal turnaround
Watch for this sign at intersections and median openings
signs.trap: The red ring and slash over a curved arrow bans U-turns only — do not confuse it with No Left Turn.

signs.name: Left turn only
signs.description: Vehicles in this lane must turn left. The arrow with the word ONLY makes the movement mandatory, not optional.
steps: Confirm you are in the correct lane early
Turn left as the arrow directs
Leave the lane before the intersection if you need to go straight
signs.trap: ONLY signs are mandatory — an answer saying you may go straight from a LEFT ONLY lane is always wrong.

signs.name: One way
signs.description: Traffic on this street moves only in the direction of the arrow. Enter and turn only that way.
steps: Turn only the way the arrow points
Never drive or turn against the arrow
Expect all lanes to flow in the same direction
signs.trap: When turning onto a one-way street, turn into the nearest lane moving in your direction — not the far lane.

signs.name: No parking
signs.description: Parking is prohibited where the sign and its arrows indicate. Briefly stopping for passengers may still be allowed unless posted otherwise.
steps: Do not park within the signed zone
Check the arrows for where the restriction starts and ends
Find a legal space beyond the zone
signs.trap: No Parking is not No Stopping — you may often stop briefly to load passengers, but you may not leave the vehicle.

signs.name: Wrong way
signs.description: You are driving against traffic, usually after entering an off-ramp or one-way street by mistake. Get out of danger immediately.
steps: Slow down and pull to the road edge immediately
Stop clear of oncoming traffic
Turn around only when it is safe
signs.trap: Wrong Way appears after Do Not Enter — by the time you see it, you must stop and turn around, not drive on to the next exit.

signs.name: No right turn
signs.description: Right turns are prohibited at this intersection. The ban applies at all times unless a plaque limits the hours.
steps: Do not turn right here
Continue straight or take another allowed movement
Plan a legal right turn at a later intersection
signs.trap: The red slash always covers the banned movement — misreading which arrow is crossed out is the common mistake.

signs.name: No left turn
signs.description: Left turns are prohibited at this intersection. Because a U-turn begins as a left turn, U-turns are usually barred here too.
steps: Do not turn left here
Continue and reroute at the next intersection
Do not attempt a U-turn instead
signs.trap: Where left turns are banned, making a U-turn instead is usually also illegal — a favorite exam follow-up.

signs.name: Keep right
signs.description: A traffic island, median, or obstruction divides the road ahead. Pass it on the right side.
steps: Move right before reaching the obstruction
Pass the island or median on its right side
Do not straddle the divider or cross to the left
signs.trap: Keep Right marks an obstruction ahead — it is not the freeway rule Slower Traffic Keep Right.

signs.name: HOV lane
signs.description: This lane is reserved for vehicles carrying at least the posted number of occupants during the hours shown.
steps: Count occupants before entering
Enter and exit only where the markings allow
Stay out if you do not meet the posted minimum
signs.trap: In California a child or infant counts as an occupant, but driving an EV solo requires a valid decal — the car alone is not enough.

signs.name: No trucks
signs.description: Trucks are prohibited on this road, usually because of weight limits, low clearance, or residential routing.
steps: Reroute now if you are driving a truck
Expect little or no truck traffic ahead
Watch for posted weight or length limits nearby
signs.trap: A red ring and slash prohibits the pictured vehicle — it does not merely warn that trucks are present.

signs.name: Divided highway crossing
signs.description: The road you are crossing is a divided highway. You must cross two separate one-way roadways with a median between them.
steps: Treat each roadway as its own crossing
Check traffic from the left, then from the right after the median
Do not stop straddling the median if the gap is too short
signs.trap: Each half of a divided highway carries one-way traffic — checking only one direction per roadway is the tested mistake.

signs.name: Do not pass
signs.description: Passing other vehicles is prohibited in this zone, even when the road ahead looks clear.
steps: Stay behind the vehicle ahead
Wait for a Pass With Care sign or a broken line
Keep a safe following distance while you wait
signs.trap: A clear road does not make passing legal here — the zone ends only at a Pass With Care sign or new lane markings.

signs.name: No turn on red
signs.description: You may not turn while the signal is red at this intersection, even after coming to a complete stop.
steps: Stop at the red light as usual
Hold your turn until the light turns green
Look for this sign mounted near the signal head
signs.trap: Normally you may turn right on red after stopping — this sign removes that permission entirely.

signs.name: Slower traffic keep right
signs.description: If you drive slower than the surrounding traffic, use the right lane and leave the left lanes for passing.
steps: Move to the right lane if driving below the flow
Use the left lanes only to pass
Return right after completing a pass
signs.trap: The rule applies even if you drive the speed limit — blocking the left lane at the limit is still tested as wrong.

signs.name: Curve left
signs.description: The road curves left ahead. Slow down before entering, especially if an advisory speed plaque is posted below.
steps: Slow down before the curve begins
Hold the middle of your lane through the bend
Accelerate gently only after the road straightens
signs.trap: A Curve sign is gradual; the sharper Turn sign (W1-1) demands a much lower speed — exams test the difference.

signs.name: Curve right
signs.description: The road curves right ahead. Finish braking before the curve so the tires only have to steer, not slow.
steps: Brake before the curve, not in it
Keep a steady wheel through the bend
Watch for oncoming traffic drifting wide
signs.trap: Braking in the middle of a curve is the classic wrong answer — all slowing should happen before you enter.

signs.name: Winding road
signs.description: A series of curves lies ahead. Expect continuous steering changes for the next stretch of road.
steps: Reduce speed before the first curve
Keep a steady, lower pace through the series
Do not pass while the road winds
signs.trap: Winding Road means at least three curves in a row — not just one bend.

signs.name: Crossroad
signs.description: A four-way intersection is ahead. Vehicles may cross your path or turn onto your road from either side.
steps: Cover the brake as you approach
Scan left and right for crossing vehicles
Be ready to yield even on the through road
signs.trap: The yellow cross warns of an intersection — do not confuse it with the round yellow railroad sign.

signs.name: Side road
signs.description: Another road joins yours from the side ahead. Watch for vehicles turning onto or off of your road.
steps: Check mirrors and cover the brake
Watch the side road for entering vehicles
Leave room for traffic slowing to turn
signs.trap: Side Road shows traffic entering from one side only — a Crossroad sign means both sides.

signs.name: T-intersection
signs.description: Your road ends ahead at a through road. You must turn left or right.
steps: Slow down as your road ends
Signal your chosen direction early
Yield to all traffic on the through road
signs.trap: At a T-intersection the ending road always yields — through traffic does not stop for you.

signs.name: Merge
signs.description: Traffic from an entrance ramp joins your road ahead. Adjust your speed or lane position to open a gap.
steps: Check your mirrors and blind spot
Adjust speed or move over a lane if safe
Let entering traffic blend in smoothly
signs.trap: Merging traffic should reach roadway speed — answers telling ramp drivers to stop and wait for a gap are wrong.

signs.name: Lane ends
signs.description: The right lane ends ahead and its traffic must merge left. Expect vehicles changing lanes in front of you.
steps: Merge early if you are in the ending lane
Yield to cars already in the through lane
Avoid racing to the end of the closing lane
signs.trap: Drivers in the ending lane must yield to traffic already in the continuing lane — not the other way around.

signs.name: Divided highway
signs.description: The road ahead splits around a median and opposing traffic will be physically separated. Keep to the right of the divider.
steps: Keep right of the median or divider
Do not cross painted or raised separations
Expect one-way traffic on your side
signs.trap: Know W6-1 from W6-2: Divided Highway Ends means two-way traffic returns with no median between directions.

signs.name: Two-way traffic
signs.description: You are leaving a one-way road and traffic ahead travels in both directions. Oncoming vehicles will share the roadway.
steps: Keep right of the center line
Pass only where markings allow it
Recheck oncoming traffic before any left turn
signs.trap: After this sign the left side belongs to oncoming cars — casual passing answers become wrong.

signs.name: Signal ahead
signs.description: A traffic signal is ahead, often hidden by a curve or hill. Be prepared to stop if it is red or has been green a long time.
steps: Slow enough to stop if needed
Watch for traffic queued at the light
Treat a long-standing green as likely to change
signs.trap: This sign is posted where you cannot yet see the signal — waiting to react until the light appears is the error.

signs.name: Stop ahead
signs.description: A stop sign is ahead but not yet visible, usually around a curve or over a hill. Begin slowing now.
steps: Start braking early
Watch for the hidden stop sign
Come to a complete stop when you reach it
signs.trap: The warning itself does not require a stop — the full stop happens at the stop sign it announces.

signs.name: Yield ahead
signs.description: A yield sign is ahead but hidden from view. Prepare to slow and give the right-of-way before you can see it.
steps: Ease off the gas now
Scan for the crossing road ahead
Be ready to stop for traffic with the right-of-way
signs.trap: The diamond warns of a yield sign coming up — it is not itself the point where you must give way.

signs.name: Pedestrian crossing
signs.description: People may be crossing the road ahead at a marked or unmarked crosswalk. Slow down and scan both curbs.
steps: Slow and scan the crossing area
Stop for anyone in the crosswalk
Never pass a car stopped at the crosswalk
signs.trap: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk — it may be yielding to a pedestrian you cannot see.

signs.name: School crossing
signs.description: The five-sided fluorescent yellow-green sign marks a school zone or crossing. Children may be near or on the road.
steps: Slow to 25 mph or the posted school speed when children are present
Obey crossing guards completely
Watch for children darting out between cars
signs.trap: The pentagon shape is used only for school signs — shape-identification questions love it.

signs.name: Bicycle crossing
signs.description: Bicycles may cross or share the roadway ahead, often where a bike path meets the road.
steps: Slow down and scan for riders
Give bicycles at least 3 feet when passing
Yield to bikes already in the crossing
signs.trap: The sign warns that bikes cross here — it does not create a bike lane or ban cars from the road.

signs.name: Deer crossing
signs.description: Deer frequently cross this area, especially at dawn and dusk. One animal is often followed by more.
steps: Slow down at dawn and dusk
Scan the road edges for movement
Brake firmly in your lane instead of swerving
signs.trap: Swerving around an animal is the classic wrong answer — brake hard and stay in your lane.

signs.name: Slippery when wet
signs.description: The pavement ahead gets unusually slick in wet weather. Traction is worst in the first minutes of rain.
steps: Slow down in wet weather
Increase your following distance
Avoid sudden braking or sharp steering
signs.trap: Roads are most slippery when rain first begins — oil floats on the surface before washing away.

signs.name: Steep downgrade
signs.description: A steep downhill grade is ahead. Brakes can overheat and fade if you ride them all the way down.
steps: Shift to a lower gear before the descent
Let engine braking control your speed
Brake in short, firm applications
signs.trap: Riding the brake pedal downhill causes brake fade — downshifting before the grade is the tested answer.

signs.name: Bump
signs.description: A raised section of pavement is ahead. Hitting it at speed can jolt the car and lighten the steering.
steps: Slow down before the bump
Hold the wheel firmly
Avoid braking on top of the bump
signs.trap: Do your slowing before the bump — braking on it unloads the suspension and reduces control.

signs.name: Dip
signs.description: A low spot in the road is ahead. Dips can hide standing water and flood quickly in rain.
steps: Slow down before the dip
Check for water pooled at the bottom
Never stop inside the dip
signs.trap: If the dip is flooded, do not drive through — even shallow moving water can float a car off the road.

signs.name: Narrow bridge
signs.description: The bridge ahead is narrower than the road but still carries two-way traffic. Shoulders may disappear.
steps: Slow down before the bridge
Center yourself in your lane
Do not pass while on the bridge
signs.trap: Narrow Bridge still has two lanes — One Lane Bridge is a different sign that may require you to yield.

signs.name: Soft shoulder
signs.description: The unpaved shoulder ahead is soft and can grab a wheel. Dropping off the pavement at speed is dangerous.
steps: Keep all wheels on the pavement
If a wheel drops off, ease off the gas
Slow down, then steer back gently
signs.trap: If you drift onto a soft shoulder, slow first and steer back gradually — jerking the wheel back is the trap answer.

signs.name: Railroad crossing
signs.description: The round yellow sign is the advance warning for a railroad crossing ahead. Look, listen, and be ready to stop.
steps: Slow down and widen your scan
Look and listen for trains in both directions
Stop 15 to 50 feet from the tracks if a train is coming
signs.trap: Round shape means railroad only — this yellow sign is the advance warning; the crossbuck at the track is regulatory.

signs.name: Hospital
signs.description: A white H on blue marks the route to a hospital. Follow successive signs to the entrance.
steps: Follow the H signs at each turn
Change lanes early for the marked turnoff
Expect ambulances near hospital driveways
signs.trap: Blue service signs only give directions — an H sign does not create a quiet zone or change the speed limit.

signs.name: Gas
signs.description: Fuel is available near the upcoming exit or turnoff. Blue signs list available services, not commands.
steps: Decide early whether you need fuel
Signal and exit where the sign directs
Use the reentry signs to return to your route
signs.trap: Service signs promise the service near the exit, not at the ramp itself — you may drive a short distance to reach it.

signs.name: Food
signs.description: Food service is available off the upcoming exit. Logo panels may show the specific businesses.
steps: Plan your stop before the exit
Follow the trailblazer signs after leaving the freeway
Rejoin the route using the entrance signs
signs.trap: Blue panels are guidance only — they do not mean the listed businesses are open around the clock.

signs.name: Lodging
signs.description: Overnight lodging is available off the upcoming exit, shown by the bed symbol on blue.
steps: Decide before the exit if you need to stop for the night
Exit and follow the lodging arrows
Choose rest over drowsy night driving
signs.trap: The bed symbol means hotels or motels, not a rest area — rest areas have their own signs.

signs.name: Rest area
signs.description: A rest area with parking and restrooms is at the next right. Use it to break up long drives.
steps: Signal early for the turnoff
Park only in the marked spaces
Take a real break if you feel drowsy
signs.trap: Drowsy drivers should use the rest area — stopping on the freeway shoulder to rest is illegal except in an emergency.

signs.name: Airport
signs.description: The airplane symbol points the way to an airport. Follow the arrows through each interchange.
steps: Follow the airport symbol at every split
Watch for lane assignments near the terminals
Expect heavy merging around drop-off zones
signs.trap: The symbol guides you to the airport — it does not mark an airport speed zone or restricted area.

signs.name: Interstate route
signs.description: The red, white, and blue shield marks an Interstate highway. Even numbers run east-west and odd numbers run north-south.
steps: Match the shield number to your planned route
Note the direction banner above the shield
Follow the shields through interchanges to stay on route
signs.trap: Even-numbered Interstates run east-west and odd-numbered ones run north-south — a classic knowledge question.

signs.name: US route
signs.description: The white shield with black numbers marks a US numbered highway, part of the national route system.
steps: Confirm the route number matches your plan
Watch for junction and turn arrows below the shield
Follow the shield at each decision point
signs.trap: Shape identifies the system: a white shield is a US route, not an Interstate — colors and shape are tested.

signs.name: State route
signs.description: Marks a state highway. In California the state route marker is the green spade-shaped shield.
steps: Follow the marker to stay on the state route
Watch for route turns at intersections
Use the direction banners to navigate
signs.trap: California's spade-shaped Route 1 marker is a route sign, not a guide panel — each state uses its own shape.

signs.name: Bike route
signs.description: This road is a designated bicycle route. Expect riders in the travel lane and give them space.
steps: Expect bicycles in the travel lane
Leave at least 3 feet when passing a rider
Check for bikes before turning or opening doors
signs.trap: Bike Route means expect bicycles — it does not ban cars and it does not force bikes onto the shoulder.

signs.name: Telephone
signs.description: Telephone service is available ahead — useful on rural routes without cell coverage.
steps: Note the location in case of emergency
Exit where the sign points if you need help
Park fully off the traveled way before calling
signs.trap: Blue means a service is available nearby — the sign does not create an emergency stopping area on the roadway.

signs.name: Tourist information
signs.description: Tourist information is available ahead: maps, routes, and local guidance at a staffed or self-serve stop.
steps: Exit where the sign points for maps and directions
Park completely off the roadway at the center
Plan your route before rejoining traffic
signs.trap: Stopping on the shoulder to check a map is the tested wrong move — use the information stop instead.

signs.name: Exit sign
signs.description: Green panels with an EXIT tab show where a ramp leaves the freeway and what it serves.
steps: Read the exit number and destination early
Move into the exit lane well in advance
Do your slowing on the ramp, not on the freeway
signs.trap: If you miss an exit, never stop or back up on the freeway — continue to the next exit.

signs.name: Exit only lane
signs.description: The yellow EXIT ONLY panel means this lane leaves the freeway at the ramp. Staying in it forces you off.
steps: Check whether your lane is marked EXIT ONLY
Move left early if you are continuing through
Commit to the ramp if you stay in the lane
signs.trap: EXIT ONLY means the lane itself departs — unlike a normal exit, you cannot ride that lane past the ramp.

signs.name: Exit speed advisory
signs.description: The yellow number on the ramp is the advisory speed for the exit curve, set for ideal conditions.
steps: Finish braking before the ramp curve
Slow to the advisory speed or less
Go even slower in rain or with a heavy load
signs.trap: Ramp speeds are advisory, but crashing above them can still violate the basic speed law — 'just a suggestion' answers are wrong.

signs.name: Mile marker
signs.description: Small green mileposts count distance along the route. Use them to track progress and report your exact location.
steps: Note the nearest milepost on long drives
Give the number when reporting a breakdown or crash
Estimate distance to your exit from the count
signs.trap: Mile markers exist for location, not navigation — in California the postmile counts typically reset at county lines.

signs.name: Destination distance
signs.description: Green distance panels list upcoming cities and the miles to each, with the nearest city on top.
steps: Read the distances at a glance, then eyes back on the road
Plan fuel and rest stops from the mileages
Set up your lane position for your destination's exit
signs.trap: The top line is always the nearest destination and the bottom the farthest — reading-order questions appear on exams.

signs.name: Freeway entrance
signs.description: Marks a proper freeway on-ramp. Use the ramp to build up close to freeway speed before merging.
steps: Enter only at marked entrance ramps
Accelerate on the ramp toward traffic speed
Merge into a gap without stopping if possible
signs.trap: Stopping at the end of an on-ramp is the classic wrong answer — merge at or near traffic speed unless forced to stop.

signs.name: HOV lane ahead
signs.description: Overhead panels announce a carpool (HOV) lane ahead along with its occupancy rule and operating hours.
steps: Read the occupancy requirement and the hours
Position early if you qualify for the lane
Stay out during restricted hours if you do not
signs.trap: Outside the posted hours many California HOV lanes open to all traffic — always check the hours plaque before answering.

signs.name: Toll road
signs.description: A TOLL banner with the route marker means the road ahead charges a fee, usually collected electronically.
steps: Decide before the split whether to take the toll route
Follow the lane signs for pass or plate payment
Never stop or back up at a missed toll split
signs.trap: Toll express lanes may still be free to qualifying carpools — read the panels, not just the word TOLL.

signs.name: Rest area 1 mile
signs.description: A rest area is one mile ahead — the safe, legal place to stop, stretch, and fight drowsiness.
steps: Decide early and signal for the exit
Slow on the ramp into the area
Nap or stretch before continuing your trip
signs.trap: The rest area, not the shoulder, is where a drowsy driver stops — shoulder stops are for emergencies only.

signs.name: Road work ahead
signs.description: Construction is ahead. Orange signs begin the work zone, where traffic fines can be doubled.
steps: Slow down as you enter the zone
Watch for equipment, cones, and workers
Merge early when lanes shift or close
signs.trap: Work zone speed limits apply even when no workers or machines are visible at the moment.

signs.name: Flagger ahead
signs.description: A flagger is directing traffic ahead with a STOP/SLOW paddle. Their signals override signs and signals.
steps: Slow down and watch for the paddle
Stop completely when it shows STOP
Proceed at reduced speed only on SLOW
signs.trap: A flagger's instructions override all posted signs and even traffic lights — obey the person, not the sign.

signs.name: Lane closed ahead
signs.description: A lane closes ahead in the work zone and traffic must merge into the remaining lanes.
steps: Check mirrors and signal early
Merge as soon as a safe gap appears
Take turns with other drivers at the merge point
signs.trap: Merging early and smoothly is expected — accelerating to beat traffic to the closure is the wrong answer.

signs.name: Detour
signs.description: The route is closed ahead; orange DETOUR signs mark the temporary path back to it.
steps: Follow each detour arrow in sequence
Trust the posted signs over your GPS
Watch for the End Detour sign to rejoin the route
signs.trap: Follow the posted detour even when a navigation app disagrees — the closure may not be in its map yet.

signs.name: Workers present
signs.description: Workers are on or next to the roadway ahead. In California, fines are doubled where workers are present.
steps: Slow well below your normal speed
Move over a lane away from the workers if possible
Keep scanning for people stepping into your lane
signs.trap: Traffic fines double in work zones with workers present — a heavily tested California fact.

signs.name: Shoulder work
signs.description: Crews are working on the shoulder rather than in your lane. Travel lanes stay open but workers are close to traffic.
steps: Stay in your lane and reduce speed
Give the shoulder extra clearance
Watch for work trucks entering from the shoulder
signs.trap: Shoulder Work means the lanes remain open — but you are still expected to slow down and move over where possible.

signs.name: Uneven lanes
signs.description: Adjacent lanes sit at different heights during resurfacing. The pavement edge between them can pull at your wheels.
steps: Avoid unnecessary lane changes
Cross the pavement edge at a steady, deliberate angle
Grip the wheel firmly over the drop
signs.trap: Drifting lazily across the height difference can snag a tire — change lanes deliberately or not at all.

signs.name: End road work
signs.description: The work zone is over. Normal speed limits and traffic rules resume beyond this sign.
steps: Resume normal legal speed
Keep scanning as traffic spreads back out
Look for the regular speed limit sign
signs.trap: Until you pass End Road Work, the reduced work zone limit still applies — even where the work looks finished.
